entry.title: Vacuum Phase Transition and Decay to Cross the Phantom Divide
entry.summary: We show that the vacuum metamorphosis model with decay fits current baryon acoustic oscillation and supernova distance data and cosmic microwave background measurements significantly better than $Λ$CDM and nearly as well as $w_0w_a$CDM with the same number of parameters. Vacuum metamorphosis with decay provides a physically motivated model of dark energy and an explanation of current cosmological data. In this scenario, non-perturbative quantum effects of a massive scalar field freeze the Ricci scalar curvature when it reaches a critical value proportional to the mass squared, inducing a phase transition in the scalar field, giving a phantom dark energy equation of state $w<-1$. After the phase transition, vacuum energy decays into light particles, providing a natural mechanism for the dark-energy equation of state to cross the phantom divide from $w<-1$ to $w>-1$, in agreement with current cosmological indications, without requiring an explicit coupling to matter.

entry.title: Minimal model of sticky collisions in modulated optical traps
entry.summary: Collisional loss of ultracold bialkali molecules is predicted to occur through photo-excitation of collision complexes. However, recent measurements in modulated optical traps report an unexpected lack of excess survival, at odds with theoretical predictions and earlier experiments. We develop a minimal quantum scattering model that treats collisions as a coherent process occurring in the presence of the modulated trap. We demonstrate that quantum reflection from the long-range potential fundamentally alters loss dynamics, removing the tension between recent experiments and predicted sticking times. This framework provides new testable predictions such as a strong dependence on collision energy, initial molecular state, and long-range interactions, that are absent in the currently used phenomenological model.

entry.title: $h/2e$ Flux Trapping without Superconductivity
entry.summary: Recently, it was shown by Komargodski and Popov [arXiv:2601.09847] that ordinary metals threaded with an Aharonov-Bohm solenoid exclusively trap either 0 or h/2e flux. The latter value is familiar in the superconducting setting, yet we find that it holds in ordinary metals as well, with no condensate or pairing necessary. We provide an analytic explanation for the flux trapping, and extend the results to the cases of finite temperature, time-reversal invariant potentials, and lattice regularization, where we find that the flux remains trapped at 0 and h/2e.

entry.title: Emergent inflation in fractional cosmology
entry.summary: We investigate the dynamics of the early universe within an emergent fractional cosmological framework generated by a measure-deformed Newtonian action, without introducing additional propagating degrees of freedom. Considering asymptotic and dynamical requirements, we construct a minimal fractional potential that, together with the time-dependent fractional kernel, generates a regular pre-inflationary stage, quasi-de Sitter inflation, a dynamically controlled exit, and a subsequent finite duration radiation-like phase. The exact solution of the reduced early-time equation is obtained in two equivalent representations, and regularity selects a unique physical branch with finite principal curvature invariants at the initial boundary. Remarkably, the same exact trajectory evolves asymptotically toward the quasi-de Sitter regime, while an exact nonlinear analysis of homogeneous Hubble deviations establishes its asymptotic attractor character within the admissible expanding sector. Inflation ends dynamically near the zero crossing of the effective fractional force, leading to controlled background-level consistency relations among the inflationary duration, the fractional parameter, the effective equation of state parameter, and the exit scale. For the physically relevant post-inflationary regime, the model admits the characteristic radiation-like expansion over a finite post-inflationary interval. These results show that a coherent sequence of regular pre-inflationary, inflationary, and post-inflationary background dynamics can emerge from a simple and unified fractional Newtonian framework without invoking an inflaton field.

entry.title: Dynamics of spinning test particles in the innermost stable circular orbit of an approximate Kerr-like spacetime with mass quadrupole
entry.summary: We study the motion of spinning test particles in a deformed, rotating spacetime described by a metric perturbed up to second order in the mass quadrupole moment. We examine how the parameters of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) --namely the radius, energy, and angular momentum-- are modified by the particle's spin, contrasting our findings with both the spinless case and standard Kerr benchmarks. By employing effective potential techniques, we consider both co-rotating and counter-rotating configurations, corresponding to parallel and antiparallel alignments of the angular momenta. Using the Euler--Lagrange formalism and Hamiltonian dynamics within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework, we derive an explicit general ISCO equation incorporating the spin and quadrupole parameters, alongside analytical expressions for the conserved orbital quantities. Furthermore, by taking the Schwarzschild, Lense--Thirring and Kerr limits within our generalized framework, we establish new ISCO equations and compact expressions for the energy and angular momentum that extend these fundamental spacetimes to the case of spinning test particles.

entry.title: Optimizing the extraction of information from redshift probability distribution functions
entry.summary: Photometric redshifts are essential for large-scale structure analyses, yet extracting optimal point estimates and reliability measures from the probability distribution functions (PDZs) delivered by modern photo-$z$ pipelines remains challenging. We introduce turboPDZ, a machine-learning framework using PDZ features and associated observables to optimize redshift point estimates and derive a data-driven reliability score. We apply it to the three independent HSC-SSP PDR3 pipelines (DEmP, DNNz, Mizuki) across Wide and Deep/UltraDeep layers. Each PDZ is compressed via PCA and combined with summary descriptors. A multilayer perceptron, optimized with Optuna under a composite objective ($σ_{\rm NMAD}$ and $η_{0.15}$), predicts $z_{\rm ml}$. A second network, trained in log-space with MAE and calibrated post hoc, yields an empirical error scale $σ_{\rm ml}$, from which the reliability score $r_{\rm ml}$ is derived via percentile ranking. Relative to catalog point estimates, $z_{\rm ml}$ improves both metrics in all six pipeline-layer combinations. Absolute median bias is smaller in four configurations and tied in two. The reliability score achieves the lowest retained-fraction AUC in 10 of 12 native pipeline-layer/metric comparisons. For the Mizuki template-fitting pipeline, catalog reliability indicators have AUC values up to about 13 times larger than those of $r_{\rm ml}$. Feature importance shows that point estimation is dominated by PCA and location statistics, whereas reliability estimation gives greatest weight to peak, PCA, and shape information. The framework is survey-agnostic, but each PDZ dataset requires its own fitted preprocessing, PCA basis, and trained models. The code will be released as a reusable Python library at \href{https://github.com/valerio-marra/turboPDZ}{github.com/valerio-marra/turboPDZ}.

entry.title: Measurement of the galaxy-velocity power spectrum of DESI tracers with the kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect using DESI DR2 and ACT DR6
entry.summary: Joint analyses of high-resolution CMB temperature maps with galaxy surveys provide a unique way to reconstruct the radial velocity field of the underlying matter distribution via the kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich (kSZ) effect. Using data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 and the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) DR2, we present radial velocity reconstructions for luminous red galaxies (LRGs), emission-line galaxies (ELGs), and quasars (QSOs). Leveraging the spectroscopic data, we are able to reliably model the foreground contamination and report a negligible impact on our main observables. We detect the velocity-galaxy cross-correlation at $17.0σ$ for LRGs, and for the first time, at $8.3σ$ for ELGs and $6.8σ$ for QSOs. We further report the first detection of the velocity-velocity correlation using LRGs at $3.1σ$, as well as the highest cumulative detection of the kSZ effect to date at $20.8 σ$. Similarly to previous results, we find a lower amplitude of the kSZ signal compared to our fiducial halo model prediction and electron profile assuming a Battaglia profile. Combining these new observables, we obtain constraints on local-type primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG): $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc} = 15.9_{-34.4}^{+34.6}$ at 68\% confidence, which represents the tightest constraint to date derived from the velocity field. The measurements presented here already exhibit lower noise on a per-mode basis than the galaxy auto-correlation on the largest scales, $k<0.004~\rm{Mpc^{-1}}$, highlighting the key role these observables will play in the context of future CMB experiments such as the Simons Observatory.

entry.title: Two gluon fusion into a $π^0$, $η$, or $η'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
entry.summary: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($π^0$, $η$, and $η'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $η$ and $η'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence (as compared to vacuum).

entry.title: Preparation of a Laughlin-like fractional Chern insulator on a superconducting quantum processor
entry.summary: Fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) are lattice analogues of fractional quantum Hall states, hosting topological order and fractionalized anyonic excitations. Their realization poses a demanding target for quantum simulation. Here, we realize a bosonic FCI on an IBM Nighthawk superconducting quantum processor using classically optimized variational circuits. We target a Laughlin-like state that is an exact zero-energy ground state of a long-range parent Hamiltonian on a torus, eliminating physical edges and providing a favorable geometry for accessing fractional quantum Hall physics in a small system. On a $4\times4$ qubit lattice, we prepare both the four-boson FCI ground state and a three-boson state hosting two quasiholes. Measurements of particle densities and correlations reproduce the characteristic structure of the target states, while reconstructed chiral magnetization currents resolve the circulating current pattern associated with the quasiholes. The preparation of these strongly correlated topological states with shallow circuits establishes a route toward the digital simulation and manipulation of fractionalized excitations, including measurements of topological invariants and anyonic braiding.

entry.title: GRB 241113B: the first SVOM and EP gamma-ray burst A soft GRB likely seen on-axis, from soft X-rays to gamma-rays
entry.summary: In 2024, two new missions were launched to detect high-energy transients. EP and SVOM aim to observe soft transients from X-ray rich gamma-ray bursts (XRR), X-ray flashes (XRF), to fast X-ray transients (FXT). GRB 241113B, the first soft gamma-ray burst (GRB) jointly detected by EP and SVOM from soft X-rays to gamma-rays (0.5--1000~keV). GRB 241113B has an $E^{obs}_{peak} \approx 35$ keV and a redshift (z) likely between 0.5 and 3.5, with $T_{90,γ} \approx 42$~s (4--30~keV). This burst can be classified as either an XRR or XRF, depending on the fluence ratio used. The afterglow is achromatic and featureless with a normal decay ($α\approx -1.40$). The prompt emission does not satisfy the shock-breakout relation, and thus a geometry comprised of a jet is preferred. However, the afterglow fitting favors a jet viewed on-axis dominated by synchrotron emission due to electrons in a slow cooling regime, interacting with a wind medium. The bulk Lorentz factor ($Γ$) indicates that the motion of the jet is ultrarelativistic ($Γ_{0}>100$), which discards the dirty fireball model. Hence, the jet baryon loading should be compatible with that of classical GRBs (C-GRBs). The prompt spectral properties of GRB 241113B ($α$, $E^{\mathrm{obs}}_{\mathrm{peak}}$, $E_{γ,iso}$) are comparable to those of XRFs/XRRs and are in the continuity of the C-GRB distributions, setting it apart from the extragalatic FXT population solely detected by EP. Hence, the SVOM mission, with the benefit brought by the instrument ECLAIRs with its high sensitivity and low energy threshold (at 4keV), is able to detect the potential $γ$-ray counterpart of soft transients also observed by EP and help to differentiate them from FXTs. The latter show the interest of the joint operation of both missions to better study the landscape of soft transients.

entry.title: Tunable Three-Body Interactions in Microwave-Shielded Polar Molecules
entry.summary: We show that microwave shielding, which enables collisionally stable ultracold polar molecules, also leads to genuine nonadditive three-body interactions comparable to the shielding interaction itself. Their magnitude, sign, and geometrical dependence can be flexibly controlled through microwave parameters and orientation. Interaction strengths can reach the ten kilohertz-scale for ultrapolar molecules in typical optical lattices. The nonadditive three-body interactions can stabilize novel many-body phases, and should be accounted for in quantum simulation with microwave shielded molecules.

entry.title: Bayesian nonparametric estimation of correlated gravitational wave detector network noise using matrix-gamma process priors
entry.summary: This paper addresses the important problem of estimating the noise spectral density of next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, such as LISA and the Einstein Telescope (ET), where cross-channel correlations must be accounted for to avoid biased parameter estimation of gravitational-wave signals. Unlike approaches that estimate test-mass and optical-metrology-system noise separately at the single-link level and then map them to the Time-Delay Interferometry (TDI) channels through known transfer functions, we develop a Bayesian nonparametric method that directly estimates the spectral density matrix of the XYZ channels, thereby accommodating additional sources of uncertainty. Our approach combines a flexible matrix-gamma process prior on the matrix-valued coefficients of a Bernstein polynomial basis expansion with a blocked multivariate Whittle likelihood. The prior guarantees Hermitian positive definiteness of the spectral estimate at every frequency. To avoid reversible-jump methods, we use an adaptive Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm for posterior sampling. The proposed framework can also be used to correct misspecified parametric noise models. Results from a simulation study and simulated correlated-noise data for both LISA and ET demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

entry.title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by overdamped vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
entry.summary: Motivated by chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS), we investigate spin polarization during molecular electron transfer through a correlated bridge in the presence of a rapidly relaxing Peierls mode. By modulating both electronic hopping and spin--orbit coupling, the mode mediates two-body spin-spin interactions, including isotropic, anisotropic, and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya exchange. We derive these interactions using an exact Lang-Firsov transformation for a four-site chiral bridge. We then include fast vibrational relaxation in the joint electron--vibration master equation and derive the reduced electronic dynamics to second order in the vibronic coupling, retaining both coherent and dissipative contributions and the finite-time buildup of the vibrational response. We test our derivation by numerical simulations, finding spin polarization accumulated at the acceptor after unpolarized injection, with nonmonotonic dependence on damping and bridge filling. Within the postulated local-loss model, our results show that rapid vibrational relaxation does not preclude spin polarization through a correlated bridge and provide a framework for assessing vibration-mediated interactions and dissipative dynamics as ingredients of CISS in molecular electron transfer.

entry.title: Exact Electron Dynamics in Linear and Chiral Cavities: Complete Field versus Single-Helicity Reduction
entry.summary: Can a chiral cavity turn a free electron into a Landau-like orbiting particle? We answer with exact solutions of three quadratic electron--cavity models in the dipole limit, valid at arbitrary coupling. A single linearly polarized mode dresses the electron mass, which delays its flight, slows the spreading of a wavepacket and entangles the packet with the cavity. The complete transverse field, with both circular helicities, keeps two commuting, gapless translations at any coupling, mode number and helicity splitting, so the electron stays ballistic and no synthetic magnetic field appears. Keeping a single helicity gives two inequivalent models that are not related by a gauge transformation: reducing before the Power--Zienau--Woolley transformation gives ballistic motion, whereas reducing after it gives a Landau-like crossed-quadrature Hamiltonian. They differ by a real uniform field $B=sλ^2/(2ω_c)$ ($ω_c$ the mode frequency, $λ$ the coupling, $s=\pm1$ the helicity). In the complete theory the frequency $ω_{-s}$ of the partner helicity, measured against $g^2=λ^2/(2ω_c)$, decides between them: the electron is ballistic for a stiff partner, and Landau-like only at the soft-partner point, through an exact canonical reorganization that holds for the active sector but not for observables such as the electron--photon entanglement. Projecting onto one helicity after the PZW transformation is therefore not by itself a mechanism for synthetic magnetism; the mode content of the cavity is.

entry.title: Local-equilibrium theory of neutrino oscillations
entry.summary: Miscidynamics describes coarse-grained neutrino transport under the assumption that flavor mixing is in local equilibrium. Here we introduce the concept of turbulent flavor-wave viscosity and develop techniques for including it in miscidynamics. This extension of the theory is necessary when neutrinos develop weak flavor instabilities as a result of astrophysical driving. The flavor-wave dispersion relation is obtained using a new and more general form of linear analysis, which does not require small flavor coherence. Flavor-wave transport is then approximated using wave kinetics and geometric optics. We hypothesize that the dynamical emergence of local oscillation invariants restricts the extent of flavor thermalization. In this view, flavor evolution is sculpted by both entropy-increasing and order-promoting factors.

entry.title: Optimizing Prompt Radio Counterpart Searches for Gravitational-Wave Events with the Deep Synoptic Array
entry.summary: Prompt millisecond-duration coherent radio emission is proposed as a counterpart to neutron-star-containing compact mergers, produced before, during, or shortly after coalescence. Its detection would probe the plasma environment, magnetic fields, remnant evolution, and emission physics of these mergers. At GHz frequencies, dispersive delays can range from fractions of a second to several seconds, requiring the telescope to be on source before or soon after coalescence. Negative- or low-latency alerts, rapid response, and optimized pointing under uncertain, evolving localizations are therefore essential. We present a framework for prompt gravitational-wave follow-up with the upcoming Deep Synoptic Array (DSA), a sensitive, fast-slewing, wide-field GHz radio array. We simulate low-latency localization sequences and embed them in a follow-up environment with elevation, field-of-view, and slew constraints. We compare a reinforcement-learning pointing policy with a baseline that slews toward the highest-probability accessible region at each step. This peak-tracking rule is a strong, interpretable baseline for initial deployment, while the learned policy provides a complementary strategy for a subset of broad, multimodal, or arc-shaped localizations. At a random merger time, 37% of events are observable above $20^\circ$ elevation; among these, $\sim90\%$ of BNS events are successfully reached and tracked using zero-noise localization maps, decreasing to $\sim75\%$ with Gaussian-noise maps. We validate the optimized pointing trajectories on prototype DSA antennas. DSA follow-up can reach a fluence sensitivity of $\sim20$ mJy ms over a representative 700-1025 MHz sub-band, probing millisecond bursts with luminosities of approximately $10^{38}$ to $10^{39}$ erg s$^{-1}$, at or below the lower end of several coherent-emission predictions for neutron-star mergers.

entry.title: Curvature-Radiation Geometries Across the Second CHIME/FRB Fast Radio Burst Population
entry.summary: We present a population-level spectral analysis of fast radio bursts from the second CHIME/FRB catalog using three curvature-radiation-motivated templates: point-source, one-dimensional bunch, and paired-bunch cavity models. Fits are evaluated with reduced chi-squared $χ^2_r$, AIC/BIC, and the Ljung-Box residual autocorrelation test. All three templates yield median $χ^2_r$ values close to unity for both repeating and non-repeating bursts. Repeaters show narrower $χ^2_r$ distributions than non-repeaters, with statistically significant but modest population-level differences. AIC favours the one-dimensional bunch model for the largest fraction of sources, whereas BIC increases the relative preference for the simpler point-source model. However, residual autocorrelation remains widespread across all models: only 15%-21% of sources simultaneously satisfy goodness-of-fit and residual-independence criteria, indicating persistent structured residuals beyond the tested templates. These results suggest that while curvature-radiation-motivated geometries capture the dominant spectral envelope of many FRBs, additional physical ingredients or spectral components are required to describe the fine-scale spectral structure of the data. The inferred coherence scales are $\sim$16-18 cm for the one-dimensional model and $\sim$25-28 cm for the cavity model.

entry.title: Triplon thermal Hall response in a honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interactions
entry.summary: We investigate triplon topology and the thermal Hall transport in a columnar valence-bond solid of a spin-$1/2$ honeycomb-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnet. Inequivalent triangular sublattices, modeled by $J_2^A\neq J_2^B$, remove inversion symmetry at nearest-neighbor bond centers and allow in-plane Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interactions. We identify the two symmetry-allowed in-plane DM vector patterns and present detailed results for the pattern parallel to the bonds including an out-of-plane magnetic field. Within a harmonic bond-operator treatment, we determine the triplon bands, their Berry curvatures and Chern numbers, and the triplon thermal Hall conductivity. The DM interaction and magnetic field generate nonzero Berry curvatures, but the numerically integrated Chern number of every isolated triplon band vanishes. Nevertheless, the energy-dependent Bose weighting of positive and negative Berry-curvature regions produces a finite thermal Hall response at nonzero low temperatures. We delimit the dilute-triplon regime in which the harmonic transport calculation is expected to be reliable. These results show that a vanishing Chern number band does not directly constrain the triplon response of a valence-bond solid. We also comment on the effects on the columnar valence-bond solid phase of a DM interaction between next-nearest-neighbor spins characterized by an out-of-plane vector pattern.

entry.title: Facets of Gravity: A journey exploring spacetime from Planckian to cosmological scales
entry.summary: What does it mean to quantize gravity, and what can a quantum theory of spacetime actually predict? This thesis explores these questions through complementary non-perturbative approaches, from the geometry of quantum spacetime to the emergence of cosmological physics. Within Causal Dynamical Triangulations, we develop observables to investigate effective topology, statistical homogeneity, and curvature in strongly fluctuating geometries, where conventional differential-geometric tools are unavailable. Tests in two-dimensional models reveal distinct coarse-graining behaviours and provide new ways to probe the emergence of familiar geometric properties. We then turn to the Functional Renormalization Group and Asymptotic Safety, developing flow invariants to characterize ultraviolet-critical surfaces and introducing Flow Invariant Neural Networks as a computational method for reconstructing them. In scalar-tensor gravity, we investigate how ultraviolet consistency conditions can constrain infrared interactions, obtaining an inflationary scenario compatible with cosmological observations. Finally, we question whether the metric must be the fundamental variable of quantum gravity. We formulate a lattice statistical approach to purely affine gravity, in which the connection is fundamental and the metric, when it exists, is emergent. Monte Carlo simulations provide exploratory results in two dimensions, while a four-dimensional homogeneous and isotropic construction yields preliminary evidence for de Sitter-like geometry and allows the study of curvature correlations. Together, these investigations develop complementary tools for studying quantum spacetime, testing its possible continuum behaviour, and connecting fundamental gravitational theories with observable physics, while identifying the conceptual and computational challenges that remain.

entry.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $γ$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
entry.summary: Identifying the astrophysical sites of the heavy rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remains one of the most prominent unsolved problems in nuclear astrophysics. Emitted $γ$-rays from the decay of unstable nuclei have been identified as a potential observable marker on both prompt and delayed timescales which could provide conclusive evidence of the presence of $r$-process activity. In this work, we identify and discuss the importance of $^{250}$Cm to the $γ$-ray spectra of remnants, showing that the decay spectrum of $^{250}$Cm dominates the $γ$-ray spectra of $r$-process ejecta across a broad timescale ($\sim$ 2,000 - 20,000 years). We highlight the uncertain nature of this spectra: $^{250}$Cm may decay via $α$-decay, $β$-decay, and spontaneous fission, but the decay branchings are not experimentally known, and each decay channel produces unique spectral lines which may be observable. We examine the potential for observation of the most prominent spectral signatures, finding that for conventional neutron star merger remnants, $γ$-ray lines will be detectable in current and future detectors only in the very near galaxy ($\sim$ 1 kpc), but other sites which could produce a larger ejecta mass may have greater observable distances. Our findings highlight the potential of actinide decay chains to indicate r-process nucleosynthesis and further underscore the necessity of measuring the nuclear properties that define their characteristic spectral signatures.

entry.title: Stars Can Quench Superradiance Around Supermassive Black Holes
entry.summary: Light scalar fields trigger an instability around rotating black holes which drives the rapid growth of high-density bound states on astrophysically short timescales---a phenomenon known as black hole superradiance. This process is usually tacitly assumed to happen independent of the local environment. Around supermassive black holes, however, orbiting stars and compact objects act as a perturbation that drains energy from the cloud, potentially preventing its formation altogether. In this work, we quantify under what conditions this happens, focusing on bound-free state transitions. We first compute the rate of energy dissipation due to gravitational interactions, finding that the superradiance growth rate almost always dominates the environmental depletion. The two rates are, however, close enough that the conclusion could be overturned once bound-bound transitions are included. Also, the environment dissipates the cloud faster than gravitational-wave emission, implying that stellar environments must be accounted for in a variety of indirect search strategies. We then investigate the impact of the scalar's quadratic couplings to nucleons and electromagnetism, showing that these interactions can greatly enhance energy dissipation, preventing the cloud's formation. This work highlights the importance of accounting for the local environment in studies of superradiance around intermediate and supermassive black holes.

entry.title: Stress-enhanced diffusion in Yukawa crystals
entry.summary: Self-diffusion in crystallized Coulomb (Yukawa) plasmas proceeds by the thermally activated formation of vacancy-interstitial pairs and the migration of these defects through the lattice, commonly known as Frenkel pairs in the materials literature. Molecular dynamics has recently resolved an Eyring law for diffusion in unstrained crystals, which we generalize to deformed crystals in this work. We simulate sheared Yukawa crystals and show that a static elastic strain exponentially enhances diffusion due to the additional elastic energy stored in the region that participates in Frenkel pair formation relative to the unstrained crystal: $D(\varepsilon)=D_0(Γ^{*})\exp[V^{*}σ/k_{\rm B}T]$, with $σ=\tfrac12μ\varepsilon^{2}$ the elastic energy density stored by the shear strain $\varepsilon$ and $V^{*}$ the activation volume. We find a single activation volume $N_{\rm act} = n_iV^{*}\simeq31$ suffices for typical astrophysical screenings with a reduction at higher screening. This suggests Frenkel pair formation requires only a brief coordination of the nearest neighbors at a thermal maximum in oscillation. Stress-enhanced diffusion supplies a microphysical mechanism for creep in strained neutron star crusts and crystallizing white dwarf cores.

entry.title: Subsonic terahertz plasmon instability in space-time plasmonic crystals
entry.summary: We investigate collective plasma-wave dynamics in a two-dimensional electron fluid subected to a travelling periodic modulation of the effective plasma velocity. Using a hydrodynamic description combined with Floquet-Bloch theory, we show that the travelling modulation acts as a moving plasmonic crystal whose band structure is governed by an effective drift velocity in the comoving frame. We demonstrate that the closure of the Bragg gap at the edge of the Brillouin zone gives rise to an exceptional point and triggers a Krein-type instability through the coupling of positive- and negative-energy modes. Analytical expressions are derived for the instability threshold and growth rate, revealing that self-amplification can occur even when the electron drift remains subsonic in the laboratory frame. Numerical simulations of the nonlinear hydrodynamic equations confirm the theoretical predictions and show the evolution towards a saturated regime dominated by a coherent Floquet-Bloch mode. These results identify travelling plasmonic crystals as a novel platform for wave amplification and non-Hermitian band dynamics in electronic fluids.

entry.title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. II. Massless particles
entry.summary: Building on Part I of this series, where we described the emergence of massive scattering states, we demonstrate how unitary lowest-weight representations $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ of the conformal group with fixed dimension $Δ$ and arbitrary integer spin $s$ contract to massless Poincaré particle representations. This requires combining the Inönü--Wigner contraction $\mathfrak{so}(2,3) \to \mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ with an infinite boost, in which case massless scattering states naturally emerge in a carrollian basis. For $Δ>s+1$, we find that $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ contracts to the direct sum of massless particles of all spins $s'\leq s$. At the unitarity bound, lower-spin states become null so that $\mathcal D(s+1,s)$ contracts to a single massless particle representation carrying the two maximal helicities $J=\pm s$. In both cases, the inner product converges to the Poincaré-invariant one after a single helicity-independent rescaling, so that unitarity is preserved throughout the contraction.

entry.title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $γ_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
entry.summary: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $γ_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_ξ$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $γ_5$.

entry.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
entry.summary: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $φ^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, Müller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $ω$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $ωτ_π\ll 1$, where $τ_π$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $ωτ_π$, since $τ_π\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.

entry.title: Resonant analogue configurations in atomic condensates
entry.summary: As a contribution to a memorial volume, we provide a comprehensive discussion of resonant configurations in analogue gravity, focusing on its implementation in atomic condensates and combining review features with original insights and calculations. In particular, we jointly analyze the analogues of the Andreev and Hawking effects using a microscopic description based on the Bogoliubov approximation. We perform a detailed study of the thermality of the Andreev and Hawking spectra for canonical black-hole solutions, finding that both can be described by a gray-body distribution to a very good approximation. We contemplate several resonant scenarios whose efficiency to enhance anomalous scattering processes is compared to that of non-resonant setups. The presence of quantum signatures in analogue configurations, such as the violation of Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities or entanglement, is analyzed, observing that resonant configurations highly increase the entanglement signal, especially for the Andreev effect. We also discuss how these results have served as inspiration for the rapidly expanding field of quantum information in high-energy colliders. Finally, we study the physics of black-hole lasers as further examples of resonant analogue structures, distinguishing three stages in its time evolution. For short times, we compute the linear and non-linear spectrum for different models. For intermediate times, we generalize the current analysis of the BHL-BCL crossover. For long times, we discuss the emerging concept of spontaneous Floquet state and its potential implications.

entry.title: FOMO-Z. Optimal galaxy classification, photometric redshifts, and reconstruction of population distributions
entry.summary: We present FOMO-Z (Flexible Optimizer of Multi-dimensional Operators and photo-$z$s), a set of statistical methods implemented in Python for galaxy classification and probabilistic inference from photometry. The methods use a reference sample with known galaxy properties. They rely on explicit, physically interpretable criteria and make no assumptions about the functional form of the color distributions. Binary selections are calibrated using either linear color conditions, particularly suited to background galaxy selection, or flexible color--color grids, seeking to maximize completeness given a threshold on purity. For probabilistic inference, the code identifies reference objects with compatible colors within photometric uncertainties to estimate each test galaxy's probability of satisfying user-defined criteria, as well as probability density functions of continuous properties such as redshift. The code also reconstructs property distributions of selected galaxy populations using photometrically similar galaxies in the reference sample. This framework supports prior weights and reference redshift probability distributions. A built-in feature-selection method identifying informative colors is also introduced. We demonstrate applications to background galaxy selection, galaxy population classification, tomographic redshift calibration, and photometric redshift estimation. The code achieves results consistent with those obtained through machine-learning approaches, such as self-organizing maps, while remaining computationally efficient, making it suitable for large photometric surveys and future Stage IV cosmological analyses. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/GiorgioLesci/FOMO-Z.
entry.arxiv:comment: Submitted to A&A. Main text: 16 pages, 11 figures

entry.title: Proof of the entropic $c$-theorem
entry.summary: We prove an entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions by constructing a $c$-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined through the relative entropy. The proof follows Casini and Huerta's, with strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy replaced by increasing differences of the mutual information, which we prove directly in the continuum from the split property and standard properties of relative entropy. The benefit of relative entropy is that every quantity we use is finite and no cutoff ever needs to be introduced. The assumptions of the theorem are only the standard axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, the split property with finite mutual information across a gap (both implied by modular $p$-nuclearity), and a finite ultraviolet bound on the resulting $c$-functions. We also note that, formally, the $c$-function is proportional to the minimal averaged null energy of a state that reproduces the vacuum correlations between the two wedges.

entry.title: Quantum Monte-Carlo study of spin-valley ferromagnetism in rhombohedral graphene
entry.summary: Recent capacitance measurements in bilayer and trilayer rhombohedral graphene reported large magnetic entropy above the Curie temperature, suggesting the formation of fluctuating local moments. Further experimental support comes from scanning tunneling microscopy experiments in rhombohedral hexalayer graphene, which directly visualized honeycomb electron-crystal order that strengthens upon heating before melting, related to the Pomeranchuk effect. Motivated by these experiments, we construct spin-valley local-moment Hamiltonians for the quarter-metal and half-metal phases. We extract their couplings from constrained Hartree-Fock calculations, and solve their finite-temperature thermodynamics with stochastic-series-expansion quantum Monte Carlo. For the quarter metal we find a continuous 2D-Ising transition at $T_c \approx 0.7$ K, an order of magnitude smaller than the Hartree-Fock estimate (~30 K) and closer to the experimental scale of a few kelvin. For the half metal, we study the field-induced magnetization as a function of temperature with and without proximity-enhanced spin-orbit coupling. When spin-orbit coupling is negligible, intervalley Hund's coupling enhances the magnetic response. Strong spin-orbit coupling, as can be induced by a neighboring transition-metal dichalcogenide, gives rise to the standard spin-canted ground state at zero temperature. Upon heating, the in-plane polarization decreases more rapidly than the out-of-plane polarization. Surprisingly, despite the itinerant nature of the electrons, local-moment models with microscopically determined couplings appear to capture key finite-temperature magnetic properties of rhombohedral graphene without any fitting.
